newsitem.title: GERMANY: French strike costs German truckers one mln DM/day.
newsitem.headline: French strike costs German truckers one mln DM/day.

text.p: The French truckers' strike is costing the German transport industry one million marks a day, Karl Heinz Schmidt, managing director of the German Transport Association, told Reuters.

Indirect damage to German industry due to production stoppages for lack of parts could be several times that amount, as about 1,000 German trucks remain stranded in France due to the strike, now in its 11th day, he added.
"Starting next week, consumers will see themselves that things like oranges, cauliflower and Christmas trees will be more expensive," Schmidt said.
The impact on the automobile industry could worsen if makers such as Volkswagen AG have to cut back production for lack of parts from suppliers in France and Spain, he said.
Other analysts tried to downplay the impact of the strike. Cornel Renfert, head of the German-French Chamber of Commerce, said it has had no significant impact on trade with Germany,
"German-French trade relations have, in principle, not been affected by this strike," Renfert said on German radio.
There have been some individual bottlenecks, but the statistical effect on the annual trade volume is likely to be under 0.5 percent, Renfert said.
He said the strike has still been too short to have grave consequences. If it were to continue another week, however, it could have a serious impact on import-export business, he said.
France's conservative government ended mediation efforts with the truckers on Thursday, declaring victory and urging the truckers to return to work.
